measure.verdict:
The 3D maps show that most of the DNA attached to sfGFP is a shorter duplex (H1). A minority feature could be longer, so this is a mixture weighted heavily toward short. The robust attached rod is the straight one leaving the sfGFP lobe, and it ends about 65 Å from the lobe surface in 3D. That is no longer than the 2D value (about 75 Å) and far shorter than the free duplex's straight segment (115 Å) or a straight 50 bp duplex (170 Å). A 3D map has no projection foreshortening, so out-of-plane tilt cannot be hiding length in the bulk population.

Every dot-on-rod map also has a weaker, kinked "far arm" that leaves a vertex about 60 Å off the lobe and runs about 100 Å further, giving a path of about 150 Å. This arm is not supported by the 2D data of the main dot classes. When I re-project the map at each particle's own pose, it predicts far-arm mass that those 2D class averages lack. Only the long-minority 2D classes 13 and 52 (about 12% of particles in A1) contain it. So the far arm is a minority (longer, kinked DNA) or contaminating density, not the bulk shape. No closed loop and no second contact with the lobe appears at any contour in any map.
measure.numbers:
Units and frame: all maps were resampled to 2.84 Å/px in a 160-voxel (454 Å) box, then low-passed to 12 Å for segmentation. I scanned contours where the main density encloses 40,000 to 120,000 Å^3; the primary contour is 65,000 Å^3 (sfGFP 33,000 plus a full duplex 32,000). If the DNA is short, this contour can only make the rod look longer, so it biases against an H1 call.

The sfGFP lobe in the NU map (J56):
- Volume 24,487 Å^3, extents 47.5 × 32.6 × 28.0 Å, peak density 6.7 times the rod's.
- In the other maps it is 18,600 to 34,500 Å^3.

The straight attached rod (measured from the lobe surface along its centre line):
- NU map: 65.2 Å median, 62.7 to 68.5 Å over all contours.
- Hetero class 0: 60 Å. RELION postprocess: 69 Å.
- The 10 class_3D maps: particle-weighted mean 64.9 Å, range 54.6 to 84.0 Å (longest are class 4 at 84 Å and class 2 at 76 Å).
- It leaves the lobe 14° off the radial direction and 26° off the lobe's long axis. Its largest kink is 23°.
- A second rod near the lobe ends at the vertex, 57 to 75 Å from the lobe surface, 32° away from the straight rod.

The far arm:
- Path length from the lobe surface: NU 151 Å, hetero class 0 154 Å, RELION 154 Å, class_3D 143 to 171 Å.
- Straight-line distance from where it leaves the lobe to its tip is 124 Å. The kink at the vertex is 52°, and the near and far parts of the path are 76° apart.
- It is present in 9 of 10 class_3D maps (92.7% of particles) at the primary contour. Class 6 (3,927 particles) has only the straight 64 Å rod; there the far arm joins only at 100,000 Å^3.
- In the NU map it is disconnected at 40,000 and 50,000 Å^3.
- Density along it is 0.75 times the near rod, with a dense spot (2.3 times) about 133 Å from the lobe surface.
- Density along the rod falls to half at 157 Å from the lobe surface in the NU map and 158 Å in hetero class 0. These values follow the far-arm path.

Free-duplex control (J39 final iteration):
- Tip to tip 174.5 Å: a 115 Å straight segment plus a 59.5 Å arm at a 45° kink.
- The _000 iteration named in the task gives 170 Å (110 + 60 Å).
- Hetero class 1: rod 98 Å past a small end lobe, 135 Å tip to tip.

Rod width: 8 Å low-pass profile width at half height is 14.2 Å (NU), 15.3 Å (hetero class 1) and 13.5 Å (free). The attached rod is as wide as free duplex, so it is duplex-like.

Pose-based checks (NU particle poses, 54,158 particles):
- I checked the pose convention independently of rod tilt: a 3D vector's projected direction must track each particle's 2D in-plane angle. The chosen convention scores 0.81 (lobe to far tip) against at most 0.34 for the other seven conventions.
- For particles from the 2D dot classes, the median out-of-plane tilt is 19.7° for the lobe-to-far-tip direction (133 Å in 3D, 125 Å projected), 31.6° for lobe to vertex, and 52° for the straight rod.
- Re-projected map against the real 2D class averages: correlation 0.89 to 0.96 per class.
- Far-arm mass relative to the near rod, predicted against observed: class 123 0.83 vs 0.11; 130 1.18 vs 0.04; 147 0.66 vs 0.00; 31 0.43 vs 0.07; 103 0.47 vs 0.03; 114 0.34 vs 0.10; 92 0.36 vs 0.09; 145 0.24 vs 0.02. Long-minority classes match: 13 is 0.45 vs 0.54 and 52 is 0.39 vs 0.35. The same masks rotated to random angles give at most 0 on the real averages.

Which particles went into each 3D set (by A1 2D class group):
- NU: 50% dot-at-end, 45% haze decoy (class 105: 15,783 particles; class 12: 8,497).
- Hetero classes 0/1/2/3: dot fraction 0.50/0.26/0.42/0.50, haze fraction 0.45/0.56/0.47/0.39.
- Every class_3D class is 36 to 56% haze.

Loop closure: none. Tunnels are 0 at every contour in every map, except one-contour rod-to-rod tunnels in class 7 (65,000 Å^3) and class 2 (100,000 Å^3). Distal rod comes no closer than 39 to 42 Å to the lobe, and each rod touches the lobe at only one patch.

34 Å helical repeat: not found. Power in the 30 to 38 Å band shows no peak; spectral peaks sit at 43 to 57 Å. Agreement between the two half maps (0.97) is driven by the low-resolution envelope and says nothing about a helix.

sfGFP rigid fit (validation only, maps unchanged): correlation 0.78 at the lobe against 0.77 to 0.78 at control spots. Correlation about the mean is 0.49 at the lobe against 0.38 at the rod midpoint and 0.42 at the distal end, so it discriminates only weakly.

Resolution: RELION postprocess FINAL RESOLUTION is 7.97 Å (CryoSPARC mask) and 10.82 Å (loose mask). CryoSPARC GSFSC 7.9 Å (tight mask); cFAR 0.17.

caveats: The particle sets are mixed. 45% of the NU particles (hetero class 0) come from the haze decoy 2D classes 105 and 12, whose averages show a dot with a separate distant object. Hetero refinement did not sort particles by 2D group (all four classes are 25-50% dot-at-end and 39-56% haze), and class_3D did not either. Hetero class 1 is not a free-rod class: it is 26% dot, 56% haze and 15% free. Every 3D map here averages these populations, so the far arm may come partly from haze-class particles or neighbouring objects.

Orientation is anisotropic (cFAR 0.17) and the object is flexible. The out-of-plane geometry of the weak far arm and of the second rod near the lobe (32° from the straight rod) is less reliable than the in-plane lengths. Those two rods probably represent a range of hinge positions rather than two fixed arms.

Length definitions differ from A1. The 3D lobe surface is the edge of a morphological-opening segmentation at the contour. The A1 2D value of 75 Å assumes a 17 Å dot radius, so the comparison carries roughly ±15 Å of definitional slack.

The free-duplex control is itself kinked in 3D (115 Å straight plus a 60 Å arm, 174 Å tip to tip). If its extra arm were real, free DNA would be close to full length. I did not run the re-projection check on the free control, so the gap between attached and free DNA is measured on the straight segments only (65 vs 115 Å).

The pose convention was chosen by an orthogonal test (tracking each particle's 2D in-plane angle), not by rod tilt, but it depends on the A1 2D poses carried through to the NU particles. The NU job holds 54,158 particles, not the 54,181 in hetero class 0.
No 34 Å helical repeat could be shown at this resolution. The half-map agreement statistic is dominated by the overall shape and is not evidence for or against a helix.
The sfGFP rigid fit discriminates only weakly between the lobe and control spots (correlation about the mean 0.49 vs 0.38-0.42). It was used for validation only; no map was modified.

The task named J39_000 as the free control, but the job's final output is iteration _003. I used _003 as the primary and also report _000 (110 + 60 Å, essentially the same). Results also use the J56_003 final iteration.

Contour levels are thresholds on the normalised 12 Å low-passed map, so the absolute enclosed volumes depend on that filtering. The QC figure (figures/qc/dotrod_3d_length.png) was made before the segment-assignment summary; that summary is in the JSON under derived_segments, and the verdict text is under interpretation.

problems: The 65 Å 'straight rod' (S) is not the rod seen in the 2D dot classes, so the 3D length the verdict quotes does not describe the bulk population. Under the pose convention the analysis validated (xyz_RT_-), S is tilted a median 52° out of plane in dot-class views, so it would project only ~52 Å from the lobe centre (~35 Å past the surface). I re-measured the real J45_030 dot-class averages (123/130/31/147/103/114/92/145): their rods end 64-96 Å from the dot centre at half level (116-132 Å at 3 sd). One object cannot be shorter in 3D (65 Å) than in its own 2D projection (~75 Å past the surface), so '65 Å, no longer than the 2D 75 Å' shows a mismatch, not agreement. The in-plane 2D rod fits better with the lobe-to-vertex-to-far-tip direction (tilt ~20-32°), cut off at roughly 80 Å from the surface.

The far arm is not 'weak'. On the 12 Å low-passed NU map, peak density along F (z 19-60, with dense spots of 53-60 at the vertex and near 133 Å) equals or exceeds S (z 22-35). RELION local resolution is 9.1-9.9 Å along F against 8.4-10.8 Å along S, and S's tip is the worst part. F is identical in half maps A and B (within ~3%) and lies inside both the refinement and FSC masks. At the threshold where only S joins the lobe, the separate V+F component is 21,051 Å^3, against 5,979 Å^3 for the S rod. The '0.75x near rod' tube average hides this.

Contour scan is degenerate. The 40k and 50k targets return the same threshold (117.26 sigma, 30,236 Å^3 main component) because the largest component jumps in size when F connects. The NU map therefore has 4 distinct contour levels, not a 3x range. S looks stable only because it ends at a density gap of about the same depth as the gap that separates F (z ~22 vs ~19).

Only F was tested; S is trusted without the same check. The re-projection test shows the 3D map is not a faithful average of the dot-class 2D data, which casts doubt on the whole map, S included. 45% of NU particles are haze classes 105 and 12, whose re-projection fit is cc 0.21 and 0.29, so their poses are essentially unvalidated. The masks enclose all arms, so reference or mask bias (noise particles aligning to the reference) could build any of S, V or F. S was never checked for predicted against observed mass or length.

The minority explanation does not add up. Long 2D classes 13 and 52 hold 1,241 + 1,013 = 2,254 NU particles (4%, not 12%). That cannot produce an arm whose peak density matches S's, so the origin of F (minority long DNA, haze-class neighbours, wrong poses or reference bias) is still unexplained.

Anisotropy bears most on the key measurement. In the J58 3DFSC, directional resolution along S is 11.1 Å (31° from the worst direction, 13 Å), against 7.4 Å along the lobe-to-far-tip direction. S's length is the least well determined feature in the map. The 7.9 Å tight-mask GSFSC is inflated by the mask; the unmasked value is 11.2 Å and the RELION loose-mask value 10.8 Å, so features are reliable only at about 10-12 Å.

The free-duplex comparison is cherry-picked. Segmentation of the free map is degenerate: distinct_lobe is false, and its 'lobe' (65x25x25 Å) is a piece of rod. Free DNA is itself kinked (45°) with a tip-to-tip length of 174.5 Å, about full length. Compared like for like on full paths, attached lobe-surface-to-F-tip is 151 Å (176 Å from the lobe centre) against 174.5 Å free: a gap of 0-23 Å, similar to the A1 2D gap (16-33 Å), not a 50-110 Å deficit. Both maps show the same kinked architecture (45-52° kink), which is consistent with F being DNA continuing on.

The class_3D lengths do not give a length distribution. These are 12 Å maps of 2.9k-7.5k particles, each 36-56% haze, and PCA did not separate populations. Per-class S values (54.6-84 Å; class 4 at 82-92 Å over all contours, class 2 at 70-81 Å) lie within the resolution and segmentation error, and the particle-weighted mean of 64.9 Å is not a population estimate.

The decisive test is missing: reconstructing from dot-class particles only and from haze particles only, using the existing NU poses (relion_reconstruct on CPU), plus a re-projection check of S's predicted length against the 2D rods. Until those exist, no 3D length should be quoted as the length of the attached DNA.
skeptics.corrected_statement:
The 3D maps alone do not settle H1 against H2. Every dot-on-rod map shows an sfGFP lobe plus a Y-shaped DNA density: a 65 Å side arm, and a kinked path through a vertex to a far tip 151 Å from the lobe surface (176 Å from its centre). The maps are NU J56, hetero class 0, the RELION postprocess and 9 of 10 class_3D maps. The far path has the same peak density and local resolution as the side arm (about 9-10 Å) and is identical in both half maps. Its length is close to the free-duplex control's own kinked 174.5 Å path.

These maps are heterogeneous and possibly reference-biased averages. 45% of the particles come from haze classes whose re-projected poses barely match (cc 0.2-0.3), the masks enclose every arm, and orientation is anisotropic (cFAR 0.17; only 11 Å resolution along the side arm's direction). The map also fails to reproduce the dot-class 2D averages. It predicts far-arm mass they lack, and its proximal side arm would project shorter than their rods. So neither the 65 Å arm nor the 151 Å path can be assigned to the bulk population from 3D.

The evidence that most attached DNA is short still comes from 2D plus the validated poses. The dot-class averages have rods ending 64-96 Å from the dot centre (half level) with no far-arm mass. Their in-plane direction is tilted only about 20-30° on average, which implies the DNA ends roughly 55-90 Å (about 80 Å typical) from the sfGFP surface in 3D. That is well short of a 170 Å duplex and favours H1, but it is provisional. The origin of the far arm is unresolved: long DNA in a minority, haze-class neighbours, or bias. Before quoting any 3D length, reconstruct from dot-class particles only and from haze particles only with the existing poses. Robust result: no closed loop and no second contact with the lobe at any contour in any map.

problems: The comparison '3D straight rod 65 Å vs 2D 75 Å' matches two different features. The analysis's own pose data give the 'straight rod' a median out-of-plane tilt of 52° in dot-class particles, so it projects only ~52 Å from the lobe centre (pose_tests.tilt.lobe_to_straight_tip). The A1 2D rod ends ~92 Å from the dot centre (75.4 + 17). The 2D in-plane angle follows the lobe→vertex / lobe→far-tip direction (Rbar 0.81), not the straight rod (0.51). The 2D rod therefore runs along the vertex/far-arm path and goes ~35 Å (projected) past the vertex. Also, a rigid 3D length that comes out shorter than its own 2D projection is not physically possible. That points to the 3D threshold length under-reading, so it is a lower bound, not a measurement.

'Far arm absent from the main 2D classes' reverses the null test. For every main dot class, the real far-arm value is above the rotated-mask null: 123: 0.11 vs -0.24±0.09; 130: 0.04 vs -0.20±0.08; 31: 0.07 vs -0.05±0.03; 147: 0.00 vs -0.08±0.02; 103: 0.03 vs -0.06±0.03; 114: 0.10 vs -0.03±0.02; 92: 0.09 vs -0.03±0.02; 145: 0.02 vs -0.03±0.01. That is ~3-7 SD above null. Measured from the null, the real averages hold roughly 10-40% of the predicted far-arm mass. So the far arm is weak in 2D, not missing. This fits a sizeable minority or flexibly blurred distal DNA, as well as contamination.

Density does not support splitting a 'robust straight rod' from a 'weak far arm'. I re-sampled the 12 Å NU map (lobe peak ~1075, tube maximum within 6 Å of each path). The weakest point on all three paths is similar: straight rod ~140, lobe→vertex ~112, vertex→far tip ~120. The vertex blob (~380) and far-end blob (~400) are denser than any point on the straight rod (maximum ~217). At the high threshold the script labels '40k', the far arm is a separate 21,051 Å^3 component, while the near rod is only ~6,000 Å^3. Whether the far arm counts as 'connected' depends on one threshold crossing (minimum ~112-120 vs ~140), not on a real difference in density.

The contour scan is narrower than reported. At '40k' and '50k' the bisection returns the same threshold (117.26 σ, actual volume 30,236 Å^3), because the largest component jumps when the far arm connects. 'Disconnected at 40,000 and 50,000 Å^3' is therefore a single threshold, and the scan has 5 distinct levels, not 6.

Flexibility is not removed by going to 3D. The attached rod is ~6.7x weaker than the lobe and drops from ~860 to ~210 within 24 Å of the lobe centre. Two near-lobe rods 32° apart (a V) are what averaging over an out-of-plane hinge looks like. A threshold/skeleton length is sensitive to hinge spread in the same way the half-max length is: A1's own calibration gives ~19-24 Å under-read at 20-25°. 3D removes projection foreshortening only for a rigid feature. So the 65 Å value cannot tell H1 (short duplex) from a full-length duplex on a flexible attachment (H3). What 3D plus the poses do argue against is H2 as a rigid, fixed-tilt full-length rod: the lobe→far-tip direction has median tilt ~20°, mean cos 0.88, so there is little foreshortening to hide length.

Selection and representativeness. Only ~27.0k of ~76.8k dot-at-end particles (~35%) ended up in hetero class 0 / NU. The others went to class 1 (~11k, 14%), the haze decoy class 2 (~17k, 22%) and the ice decoy class 3 (~21.5k, 28%). 'Most of the DNA attached to sfGFP' is therefore inferred from about a third of the dot particles, diluted by 45% haze particles that fit the map badly (cc 0.21 / 0.29). My component check shows the class 1 and class 2 maps (together ~36% of dot particles) as ~100 Å elongated rods with no distinct lobe. Class 2 was never analysed. Hetero refinement did not sort by 2D group, so each map's shape partly reflects its seed volume rather than a subpopulation. Class 1, seeded from the free rod, reproduces the free control (~100 Å rod plus a separate compact blob of equal peak).

The task's premise that ~31k dot-on-rod particles moved into the free-rod class is wrong according to the composition. Class 1 holds ~11k dot particles, ~24k haze and ~6k free. The analysis flagged this correctly, but it then gives no reason to exclude class 1's ~100 Å rod from the attached-length picture for those ~11k dot particles.

Free-control comparison. In my check the free J39_003 '59.5 Å arm' is a compact globular blob (~21x15x15 Å at 0.35·max, peak 0.87 of the rod peak), not a duplex arm. The free rod itself is ~113-118 Å, matching the 2D 109 Å. Free DNA is therefore ~115 Å, not 170 Å, so 170 Å is the wrong yardstick. Also, the NU path from lobe centre to far tip (176 Å) almost equals the free tip-to-tip distance (174.5 Å). If the far arm is real, that cuts against H1, and the verdict does not mention it.

A like-for-like length estimate gives a smaller gap than 65 vs 115 Å. Taking the 2D-visible rod (75 Å past the surface) along its pose-validated direction (median tilt 20-32°, mean cos 0.79-0.88) gives ~85-95 Å in 3D. Against ~109-115 Å for free DNA, the gap is ~15-30 Å, not ~50 Å.
skeptics.corrected_statement:
The 3D data do not separate H1 from a full-length duplex on a flexible attachment (H3). They do argue against H2 as a rigid full-length duplex hidden by a fixed out-of-plane tilt. Under the validated pose convention (Rbar 0.81), the direction the 2D dot-class rod follows (lobe→vertex→far arm) is tilted only ~20-32° (mean cos 0.79-0.88) in those particles. Foreshortening therefore accounts for ~10-20 Å at most.

Deprojecting the 2D attached length (75 Å past the surface) gives ~85-95 Å. Free duplex measures ~109 Å in 2D and ~115 Å in 3D (rod segment). The attached DNA in the dot-at-end population is probably still somewhat shorter, by ~15-30 Å, which is the A1 2D range. That leans toward H1 but is not decisive.

The 65 Å 'straight rod' should not be used as the attached length. It is strongly tilted in dot-class particles (projects to ~52 Å from the lobe centre, far less than the ~92 Å 2D rod), so it is not the feature seen in 2D. Its end is a threshold crossing on density ~6.7x weaker than the lobe. The near-lobe V (two rods 32° apart) points to hinge averaging. On density alone it cannot be told apart from the 'far arm': both have weakest points ~110-150 against a lobe peak of ~1075, and the vertex and far-end blobs are denser than the straight rod.

The far arm (~150 Å path) is weak but not absent in the main 2D dot classes. Its signal there is 3-7 SD above the rotated-mask null, about 10-40% of the predicted mass. It is strong in the long-minority classes 13 and 52. It is consistent with a minority of longer, kinked DNA, flexibly blurred distal DNA, or neighbouring-particle density from the 45% haze particles. These data cannot choose between them.

The 3D maps represent only ~35% of the dot-at-end particles, mixed with 45% haze. The remaining dot particles sit in hetero classes that did not sort by 2D group. Two of those classes (~36% of dot particles) refined to ~100 Å rod-like maps resembling their seeds.

Robust conclusions:
- No closed loop or second lobe contact at any contour in any map.
- Rigid tilt does not explain the 2D shortening.
- Attached DNA length is ≤ free length, with a 2D-derived gap of ~15-30 Å. The 3D maps do not pin down this gap further, and 3D did not resolve H1 vs flexible H3.

The free DNA itself is ~115 Å, not 170 Å, so 'full length' in this sample means ~110-115 Å.
